\chapter{Synthesis --- Supposing Out Loud}
\label{ch:sintesis-condiciones}
\hlchaptermodality{210}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can speak about a world that does not exist.}

I can speak about a world that does not exist.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{Synthesis — supposing out loud}

\label{lesson:ES-C56-sintesis-condiciones}



\begin{quote}
Build the supposing form of \emph{ser}. (\emph{Fuera}.) Of \emph{hacer}. (\emph{Hiciera}.)

Now use one.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Say these, and hear how much each one carries:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Si fuera profesor, hablaría español todos los días.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Si tuviera tiempo, comería en casa.}
\end{quote}

Each says what would happen \textbf{and} that it is not happening, in one breath and with no extra words. English needs \emph{but I'm not} to be quite that clear; Spanish puts it in the verb endings.

\textbf{This is the first thing in this book you can say about a world that does not exist.} Everything before it described what is, was, or will be.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: what the climb cost}]
Look back at what this one sentence needed.

It needed \emph{si}, which cost one chapter. It needed the \emph{-ría} form, which you had already. And it needed the supposing form — which needed the \textbf{preterite plural}, a gap nobody would have named as the thing standing between you and hypothetical speech.

That is worth remembering the next time something in this language looks arbitrary. The order things must be learned in is rarely the order they look important in.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Si fuera profesor, hablaría español todos los días}
  \item an unreal condition of your own
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What can you now say that you could not before? (Something about a world that \textbf{is not the case}.) And what had to be built first? (The \textbf{preterite plural} — and nobody would have guessed it.)
\end{tcolorbox}
